messages:
dana: @mike customer (BioHealth) reports missing audit logs from their Private VPC deployment. They see KMS 403s and audit-forwarder backlog growing since Feb 14. Can we triage?

mike: saw ticket. can you paste the exact errors they shared?

dana: From their node logs: 'audit-forwarder: failed to send event: 403 Forbidden from kms.company.com:443 - AccessDenied' and 'audit-shipper retrying, backlog=12000'. Also SDKs show repeated retries and increased latency.

security-bot: Automated alert: increased audit-backlog > 10k for org=biohealth cluster=cluster-prod-3. Linked incident INC-8123.

ash: are they going through a corporate egress proxy or NAT gateway? curious if TLS inspection is in play.

dana: yes, customer routes egress through corp HTTP proxy that does TLS inspection. they say kms endpoints were "allowed" but HSM management endpoints may be blocked by a recent policy change.

mike: quick repro commands for support to run on a node:
```
curl -v https://kms.company.com/health -H 'Host: kms.company.com'
openssl s_client -connect kms.company.com:443 -servername kms.company.com
```
run those and paste output. also check for client certs if HSM management uses mTLS.

ash: also check iptables/nft and DNS: `sudo iptables -S OUTPUT`, `sudo nft list ruleset`, `dig +short kms.company.com`, and `/etc/hosts`. if dns resolves to internal proxy IP that's a clue.

dana: customer ran curl and got `HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden`. openssl shows the TLS handshake completes but `ServerName` seen by backend was `proxy.host.internal` (proxy replacing SNI). KMS rejects because SNI must match and client cert is stripped.

mike: yeah this is a TLS-inspection break: KMS/HSM endpoints require original SNI and in some cases client-certs (mTLS). proxies that terminate TLS or rewrite SNI will cause 403. fix is to bypass TLS inspection for kms.company.com (allow TCP passthrough) or explicit proxy bypass by host/IP + SNI.

ash: add these repro steps for support doc:
1) tcpdump during curl: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host kms.company.com -w /tmp/kms.pcap`
2) run `curl -v` from node and attach pcap + curl output
3) collect `sudo ss -ntp | grep 443` and `sudo iptables -S`
4) check proxy logs for replaced SNI / client cert stripping

dana: customer also reported billing spikes because some requests fell back to hosted endpoints and retried rapidly. recommend fail-closed: do not reroute audit streams to hosted as an automatic fallback; queue + alert instead.

mike: owners: @ash to draft proxy+firewall guidance for Private VPC customers, @sre-oncall to update runbook and probes, @dana to coordinate with the customer and CS. ETA: EOD tomorrow for a first pass.

sre-oncall: :thumbsup: i'll add a KMS handshake probe to private-vpc runbook (check SNI + 200) and include sample nft/iptables rules and a sample proxy-bypass stanza.

security-bot: Action logged: linked INC-8123, severity=high, compliance-impact=audit-loss. Reminder: escalate to Compliance if backlog > retention window.

dana: temporary workaround sent to customer: bypass proxy for `kms.company.com` and allow egress to IP range `143.32.12.0/24` (their KMS egress). after they applied bypass the backlog started draining.

ash: follow-up note: ask customer to confirm HSM management endpoints (port 8443) also bypass proxy and preserve client certs. if using HSM, mTLS cannot be inspected.

mike: final follow-up: add an automated weekly check from private clusters that connects to kms.company.com verifying SNI and 200 OK; alert and auto-open INC if failure. also add guidance to Sales/SEs for new Private VPC onboarding about proxy/TLS-inspection requirements.

dana: thanks all — i'll update the support ticket with repro steps, workaround, owners, and timeline. will post a short summary to #customer-success after customer confirms.
